source_work: Noah Webster, An American Dictionary of the English Language (1828)
rights_basis: The original 1828 dictionary text is public domain.
transcription_source: Internet Archive OCR checked directly against the corresponding 1828 printed page images.
selection_method: Selected ordinary KJV study vocabulary from the unresolved K-L inventory, excluding biblical names already supported by Easton or Nave and compounds without a defensible printed Webster target.
review_method: Compared every retained entry with the original printed page image, corrected OCR substitutions and broken words, preserved Webster's wording and sense order, expanded abbreviated parts of speech, language names, and Scripture book names for display, and recorded KJV spellings, inflections, and closed compounds as lookup relationships rather than inventing headwords Webster did not print.

deferred_candidates.reason: No standalone LONG-WINGED headword was found in the reviewed alphabetical sequence; retain the existing passage-specific rare-term help rather than force a partial alias.

verified_lookup_relationships.relationship: KJV closed compound mapped to Webster's LEAN adjective sense, which defines wanting flesh
KJV second-person past-tense form mapped to Webster's LAY
Plural noun form mapped to Webster's singular LANCET
KJV first element of the printed compound LIGN-ALOES mapped to Webster's full headword
KJV historical spelling mapped to Webster's LOWER sense meaning dark, gloomy, or threatening a storm

additional_resolved_forms.resolution: Direct lookup resolved from the reviewed LATELY headword
Direct lookup resolved from the reviewed LINEAGE headword
